chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman whom a man marries in mut'ah (temporary marriage), then her husband dies. Is there a waiting period ('iddah) upon her? He said: She observes a waiting period of four months and ten days. And if she stays with him for days, she observes the waiting period and also observes mourning (hudd). I said: Does she observe mourning? He said: Yes, if she stayed with him for days, she observes the waiting period and also observes mourning. And if she was with him for one day or two days or an hour of the day, then the full waiting period is obligatory upon her and she does not observe mourning.

key_terms.حَيْضَةٍ وَنِصْفٍ: Three menstrual cycles (or three months for non-menstruating women)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and mourning duration for a woman in temporary marriage after her husband's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between 'iddah (waiting period) and hudd (mourning period) for women in temporary marriage (mutah) upon their husband's death, a key topic in Shia fiqh. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that while cohabitation for a significant duration necessitates both, brief encounters (even a single hour) only require the full 'iddah without the mourning period, reflecting the principle that mourning is tied to the depth of marital bond established through sustained residence.
